us-0Q5f.title: Oil pumpjacks: short industrial pumps
us-0Q5f.summary: Oil pumpjacks are short metal machines that pump oil. Most common in western states, especially Texas, eastern New Mexico and North Dakota.

us-0Th8.title: Google car: Gen 2 is rare
us-0Th8.summary: Gen 2 (old, low-quality) coverage is rare. In North America it points more to Canada, except Alaska, some of Hawaii and rarely the rural Deep South. Gen 3 is also much less common than in Canada.

differs.how: Gen 2 and Gen 3 are much more common there

us-0fzw.title: Restaurants: Carl's Jr. vs Hardee's
us-0fzw.summary: Same company and similar logos. Carl's Jr. is on the West Coast and in the Southwest, Hardee's in the centre and east. Wyoming and Oklahoma have both.

us-177u.title: Crops: short yellow canola flowers
us-177u.summary: Fields of short yellow canola flowers are common along the northern border, rarely in the next state west.

us-1Iuf.title: Buildings: bright art deco near the coast
us-1Iuf.summary: Miami and Miami Beach have many historic, multi-storey art deco buildings painted in bright colours near the coast.

us-1MNA.title: Gas station: Kum & Go
us-1MNA.summary: A gas station chain based in Iowa, with pockets in the Ozarks, Colorado, Wyoming and North Dakota.

us-1agU.title: Road: rumble strips along the edges
us-1agU.summary: Highways and some state roads have rumble strips (small dents across the pavement) on the edges and between lanes. They are much rarer in Canada.

differs.how: Rumble strips are much rarer there

us-1p2i.title: Landscape: temperate rainforest, ferns
us-1p2i.summary: Coastal rainforest with broadleaf trees, huge conifers and ferns, in the northwest. It continues north into coastal Canada and Alaska.

us-2pAs.title: Driving side: left, in one Caribbean territory
us-2pAs.summary: The US Virgin Islands are the only part of the US that drives on the left.

us-3KOY.title: Sign: white metal plate reading E-2
us-3KOY.summary: In New Hampshire, a white metal sign with "E-2" often stands beside the road, usually at either end of bridges.

us-3Trb.title: Gas station: Sheetz
us-3Trb.summary: A regional gas station and convenience chain in the mid-Atlantic and central Appalachians, with the most in Pennsylvania.

us-45FS.title: Landscape: north-south mountain wall by big cities
us-45FS.summary: In central Colorado, a large north-south ridge divides the Rockies in the west from the Great Plains in the east, next to the big cities.

us-4eeS.title: Supermarket: H-E-B
us-4eeS.summary: A supermarket found only in Texas, mostly in big cities.

us-5T1y.title: Landscape: eroded sand-brown rock with trees
us-5T1y.summary: A park in North Dakota with eroded sand-brown rock like Badlands, but with more trees on it and almost all coverage in fall colours. Similar formations appear in far eastern Montana.

us-5lk0.title: Crops: corn fields
us-5lk0.summary: Corn fields are most common in the regions shown on the map, mostly the Midwest.

us-5v2z.title: Sign: county road lettered A to ZZZ
us-5v2z.summary: Only Wisconsin and Missouri letter their county highways (A to ZZZ). Wisconsin signs usually say "County" above the letter, Missouri's usually don't.

us-5zZB.title: Buildings: very large sloped roofs
us-5zZB.summary: Buildings with very large sloped roofs are most common in Oklahoma, Texas and Louisiana, and to a lesser degree nearby states.

us-6HTI.title: Bollard: square reflector
us-6HTI.summary: Square reflector bollards are common in Utah, Arizona and Idaho. Utah's usually has 2 bolts, Arizona's one, Idaho both. Diamonds turned on their side look like squares.

us-6MhQ.title: Gas station: Kwik Trip
us-6MhQ.summary: A gas station and convenience chain in Wisconsin and Minnesota. In Iowa it is called Kwik Star with similar branding, and some are called Stop-N-Go.

us-70s3.title: Houses: small rectangular mobile homes
us-70s3.summary: Small, rectangular mobile (trailer) homes are popular in rural areas, most common in the southeast. They are seen in Canada far less.

us-71B8.title: Houses: on stilts near the coast
us-71B8.summary: Stilt houses appear on the coast, especially towards the south and on the Atlantic and Gulf coasts.

us-785L.title: Landscape: mesas and tablelands, red rock
us-785L.summary: Southwest desert with many mesas and tablelands. The rock is often red, and red soil is common.

us-7c7R.title: Flags: each state has its own flag
us-7c7R.summary: All 50 states have their own flag, and the more distinctive ones appear more often.

us-7hxg.title: Restaurant: In-N-Out Burger
us-7hxg.summary: A regional fast food chain in the Southwest, with about two thirds of the locations in California.

us-7kSA.title: Landscape: dry sandy treeless mountains
us-7kSA.summary: Death Valley National Park: dry, sandy, treeless mountains beside the roads, and in Gen 3 coverage a particularly dusty sky. Many smaller roads only have Gen 1.

us-7mOi.title: Marker: small green and red bridge-end signs
us-7mOi.summary: Small green and red rectangular signs mark the ends of bridges and guardrails in Maine, New Hampshire and Massachusetts, though not on every one.

us-8jCA.title: Guardrails: brown painted in national parks
us-8jCA.summary: Guardrails, signs and posts painted medium brown mark national parks, often in the west. The rails may be wood or metal, and rock walls sometimes replace them. Exceptions exist.

us-95HC.title: Bollard: plain white post with black reflector
us-95HC.summary: Simple white bollards with black reflectors, unique to Wisconsin.

us-BP7h.title: Landscape: dry rocky peaks, yucca, prickly pear
us-BP7h.summary: Big Bend National Park in southwest Texas on the Mexican border: dry rocky peaks and shrubs, with yucca and prickly pear of the Chihuahuan desert.

us-CZYl.title: Shops: gas station chains not found in Canada
us-CZYl.summary: A set of gas station and convenience store chains that operate in the US but not in Canada. Not a full list, just the most common.

us-CeHA.title: Street sign: black with white text
us-CeHA.summary: Black street signs with white text are common at intersections in South Carolina.

us-Cusb.title: Bollard: black paddle-shaped post
us-Cusb.summary: Black bollards with a paddle-shaped body, common in Utah and Wyoming and also in Nebraska. A square white reflector on this design is found only in Wyoming.

us-DYNm.title: Roadside: short rock walls
us-DYNm.summary: In rural Connecticut, Rhode Island, Massachusetts and New Hampshire, short rock walls often run beside the road. They rarely appear in neighbouring states.

us-EG9C.title: Restaurant: Pizza Ranch
us-EG9C.summary: A restaurant chain in the middle of the country, with the most in Iowa and Minnesota.

us-EPc4.title: Landscape: vineyards, olive trees, edge hills
us-EPc4.summary: A large valley with a Mediterranean climate: vineyards and olive trees, and rolling hills near its edges.

us-EhSf.title: Bollard: three round reflectors
us-EhSf.summary: Bollards with three circular reflectors are common in New Mexico.

us-EuM3.title: Houses: very narrow one-storey wooden shotgun
us-EuM3.summary: Very narrow, one-storey wooden shotgun houses are most common in and around New Orleans, Houston, Louisville and in Mississippi.

us-FNeR.title: Bollard: dark metal post
us-FNeR.summary: In Colorado and Wyoming: a dark metal post whose white circular reflector sits below the top, so part of the post sticks out above. A white or grey painted top is unique to Wyoming.

us-FU8a.title: Road lines: yellow centre, white edges
us-FU8a.summary: Yellow middle lines, usually double, and white edge lines. On divided roads the edge line next to the median is yellow. Canada has fewer double centre lines, but not rarely, so be careful.

differs.how: Double centre lines are less common there

us-FmvU.title: Google car: black roof, red hood Ford Bronco
us-FmvU.summary: A Ford Bronco with an unblurred black roof and red hood, mostly on unpaved rural roads from Oregon to North Carolina. Looking back you see two other Ford SUVs escorting it.

us-FrXC.title: Landscape: low rolling hills, lakes and fields
us-FrXC.summary: Between two cities in central Florida there are low rolling hills, lakes and farmland, the only main hilly area in central or southern Florida.

us-Fz62.title: Supermarket: Hy-Vee
us-Fz62.summary: A supermarket common in the Upper Midwest: Iowa, Minnesota, Wisconsin and Illinois.

us-GvVV.title: Road line: snowplowable markers shaped like H
us-GvVV.summary: Snowplowable raised markers, built into the road and a bit like the letter H, only on highways in the eastern states on the map.

us-HIKl.title: Signpost: black-and-white horizontal marker on stop post
us-HIKl.summary: On some rural stop sign posts in Minnesota, a black-and-white marker is fixed horizontally. The shape varies slightly.

us-Hbiu.title: Road line: black stripe between double yellows
us-Hbiu.summary: In California, a black stripe sometimes shows between the two yellow centre lines.

us-HdxL.title: Road: grainy salt-and-pepper surface
us-HdxL.summary: A grainy, salt-and-pepper road surface is common in the biggest southern state. Similar pavement sometimes appears in neighbouring states.

us-IFHA.title: Houses: wooden shingle walls
us-IFHA.summary: Coastal New England houses often have shingle walls: layered, overlapping wood panels. A similar panelling is seen over a wider area.

us-IJog.title: Road works: orange barrels with white stripes
us-IJog.summary: Orange plastic construction barrels with horizontal white stripes and a black rubber base, used to close lanes.

us-IXin.title: Mailbox: on a post with a side flag
us-IXin.summary: A mailbox on top of a post with a small flag on the side, mostly seen in North America.

us-IcHf.title: Sign: warning signs full of words
us-IcHf.summary: Signs use lots of words, e.g. railway crossing signs say "railroad crossing" and yellow diamonds carry text. In Canada the crossing sign is blank and words go on a plate below the diamond.

differs.how: Canadian crossing signs are blank, words go on a plate below

us-Ir2p.title: Traffic lights: hanging on long bars with signs
us-Ir2p.summary: At big intersections, long metal bars hang over the street with traffic lights, and often street or highway signs, attached. Canada has this too.

us-J9Ng.title: Plants: sagebrush, short blue-green shrub
us-J9Ng.summary: A short, shrubby, blue-green bush common in the dry interior west.

us-JWKa.title: Landscape: mountains west, low land east
us-JWKa.summary: Most high ground is in the west: big mountain ranges and high flat plateaus, with lower valleys such as the Central and Imperial valleys. The east is much lower, with the Appalachians as the main uplands.

us-JWY6.title: Lawns: beige in winter in the south
us-JWY6.summary: Southern lawn grasses go dormant in winter, so lawns turn beige or light brown. Northern grasses stay much greener.

differs.how: Bermuda grass is common there too

us-K29K.title: Road: thin, long rumble strips on edges
us-K29K.summary: Some Kentucky roads have rumble strips shaped as thin, fairly long recessed lines at the very edge of the road.

us-Khhw.title: Fences: dark wooden with horizontal supports
us-Khhw.summary: Dark wooden fences with several horizontal rails are common in farming areas of the central and southern Appalachians, Pennsylvania to Georgia. They appear elsewhere less.

us-Kijw.title: Houses: pale stucco with red clay-tile roofs
us-Kijw.summary: Spanish Colonial Revival buildings with light stucco walls and red clay tile roofs, in the desert southwest (California, Nevada, Arizona, Texas) and similar ones in Florida and coastal Georgia.

us-LBiS.title: Marker: white and orange fibre-optic cable post
us-LBiS.summary: White and orange fibre-optic cable markers are almost unique here, though very rarely seen in Canada.

us-LduI.title: Google car: Gen 3 without antenna
us-LduI.summary: Gen 3 coverage usually shows no antenna, which helps tell it from Europe. National parks have a Gen 3 car with a stubby antenna with diagonal coils around it.

us-MT0w.title: Plate: short plates, no blue strip
us-MT0w.summary: Short licence plates, unlike Europe's long ones with a blue strip. Each state has its own design.

us-NHlY.title: Landscape: reddish soil
us-NHlY.summary: Many parts of the Deep South, from Oklahoma to South Carolina, have reddish soil, from yellow to deep red.

us-NrjG.title: Guardrail: square legs with bar across the top
us-NrjG.summary: Square guardrails, a long top bar held up by square legs, are the main type in New York and Wyoming, and appear less in nearby states.

us-OEtX.title: Sign: yield triangle with the word YIELD
us-OEtX.summary: Upside-down triangle with a red border, white middle and the word "YIELD". Canada's looks similar but has no text.

differs.how: Canadian yield sign has no text

us-Okab.title: Signs: blue and yellow county road shields
us-Okab.summary: Blue and yellow shields mark county roads in certain states. Some counties have unique designs.

us-PJKL.title: Signpost: yellow or red reflective bands
us-PJKL.summary: Yellow or red bands often wrap around signposts in Texas. Similar reflectors appear in other states such as Hawaii.

us-PPTf.title: Gas station: Buc-ee's, huge with many pumps
us-PPTf.summary: An oversized gas station with many rows of pumps and a very large store. Mainly in Texas, rare in nearby states.

us-PWG0.title: Landscape: tropical islands on a single-lane highway
us-PWG0.summary: A chain of tropical islands: the road is usually single-lane, with green tropical plants beside it and white sandy soil. Towns have more planted palms and mowed grass.

us-Pvk9.title: Sign: small green with three rows of numbers
us-Pvk9.summary: New York and Vermont have small green signs with three rows of numbers. The top row is the road number. Vermont's second row almost always starts with 0, New York's starts with a transport district number.

us-QHSQ.title: Pole: thick yellow horizontal plates
us-QHSQ.summary: Thick yellow horizontal metal plates with raised or black lettering, alone or several per pole. Found in Oregon, eastern Idaho, Utah and Wyoming, less commonly in California and Washington.

us-R1je.title: Pole: white plate with orange rectangle
us-R1je.summary: A rectangular white metal plate with an orange rectangle and diamond is on most poles in Wisconsin and Michigan's Upper Peninsula.

us-R6mQ.title: Sign: green ATV route sign
us-R6mQ.summary: Green ATV Route signs are unique to Wisconsin.

us-RIXH.title: Houses: colourful shotgun houses
us-RIXH.summary: Neighbourhoods around New Orleans have many colourful shotgun houses, and the centre has colourful buildings with second-floor wrap-around balconies.

us-RO1J.title: Restaurants: chains not found in Canada
us-RO1J.summary: A set of restaurant chains that operate in the US but not in Canada (Chick-fil-A has a few locations near one Canadian city). Not a full list.

us-S13A.title: Street sign: with street numbers and arrows
us-S13A.summary: North Carolina often has street signs that show street numbers and arrows as well as the name. Other states have similar ones occasionally.

us-SmGr.title: Landscape: rocky shrubby peaks, pink-red rock
us-SmGr.summary: A small area in southwest Oklahoma with rocky, shrubby peaks. Some are tree-covered and the rock has a pinkish red tint.

us-SykO.title: Language: US spelling (center) and miles
us-SykO.summary: English with American spelling (center, color) and imperial units: miles, plus feet and inches on bridge heights. Helps tell it from English-speaking Canada.

differs.how: Canada uses British spelling and mostly metric

us-SyqR.title: Sign: big green highway signs, curved edges
us-SyqR.summary: Large rectangular green metal signs with curved edges and white text show exits, distances and road names. Canadian highway signs look similar but have square edges.

differs.how: Canadian highway signs have square edges

us-TM60.title: Trees: palms on southern coasts and in deserts
us-TM60.summary: Palm trees are common on southeastern coasts and in the desert southwest. The Mexican fan palm is common in California and along the Gulf Coast.

us-TrbD.title: Marker: yellow sign with black vertical triangles
us-TrbD.summary: In Minnesota, yellow signs with vertical black triangles mark most major river crossings and the start and end of guardrails on large highways.

us-Tunp.title: Crops: cotton, fluffy white fields
us-Tunp.summary: Large fields of fluffy white cotton, mostly in coastal southeastern states, the lower Mississippi valley, west Texas and parts of California and Arizona. Young cotton looks greener.

us-U1Mv.title: Sign: horizontal driveway sign with town and road
us-U1Mv.summary: A horizontal blue, red or green sign at the end of driveways in Wisconsin and Michigan's peninsula, with the house number plus usually the town and road name. Nearby states have similar markers but only numbers.

us-UIK0.title: Restaurant: Tim Hortons
us-UIK0.summary: The most popular chain in Canada, but with many US locations too, mostly in states bordering Ontario and Quebec, plus a few in Texas and Georgia.

us-Uwv0.title: Houses: colourful Victorian rows, bay windows
us-Uwv0.summary: San Francisco has Victorian row houses with bay windows, turrets and ornate details, built close together and often colourful.

us-Vjto.title: Signpost: thin metal with holes or U-profile
us-Vjto.summary: Thin metal signposts with several small holes or a U-shaped profile are common.

us-VoyH.title: Road line: extra thick yellow centre line
us-VoyH.summary: Some roads in West Virginia, Maryland, Delaware and Virginia have yellow centre lines thicker than usual. Not on every road, and it appears elsewhere, so combine with other clues.

us-W2CQ.title: Crops: soybeans, short dark green rows
us-W2CQ.summary: Short, dark green crops in long rows, grown where corn is: the eastern plains, Midwest, lower Mississippi valley and parts of the mid-Atlantic.

us-Wa4g.title: Sign: green plate with 3 rows of numbers on stop sign
us-Wa4g.summary: In Oklahoma, a green rectangle with three rows of numbers is often fixed to the back of rural stop signs.

us-WfNn.title: Buildings: dark wooden boards, metal roofs
us-WfNn.summary: Buildings in the interior west often use lots of dark wooden boards and timbers, and high-altitude ones often have metal roofs to shed snow.

us-WgiF.title: Highway numbering: even runs west-east
us-WgiF.summary: Interstate highways are divided roads. Even numbers run west to east (lowest in the south) and odd numbers south to north (lowest in the west). US Highways use roughly the opposite numbering pattern.

differs.how: Mexico uses different highway numbers and shields

us-Wlwb.title: Landscape: extremely tall steep peaks
us-Wlwb.summary: Glacier National Park in Montana on the Canadian border: very tall, steep peaks, with mostly hazy summer coverage. Other Rocky Mountain parks look similar.

us-WtoH.title: Landscape: dry rocky hills, yucca, live oaks
us-WtoH.summary: Dry, rocky hills with lots of yucca and prickly pear. Live oak is the main tree. West of two big cities in the south.

us-WxTi.title: Phone numbers: 3-digit area code first
us-WxTi.summary: Phone numbers start with a three-digit area code. They aren't grouped by first digit but are worth learning.

us-XV66.title: Road line: yellow lines with a wide gap
us-XV66.summary: Yellow centre lines with a noticeably larger gap between them, most common in a handful of southern states and one northwestern state. They appear rarely elsewhere.

us-XccN.title: Landscape: flat plains with few trees
us-XccN.summary: The Great Plains run through the middle of the country, from the Canadian border to central Texas. Mostly flat with few trees: some farm fields, some dry grassy land.

us-Z4Ew.title: Bridges: bright yellow steel bridges
us-Z4Ew.summary: In Pittsburgh, big steel bridges are often painted bright yellow, and the city is flanked by three rivers and steep bluffs.

us-ZU6s.title: Google car: mirrors blurred as a single peak
us-ZU6s.summary: In Gen 3 coverage, the blurred side mirrors usually form one peak. Canadian Gen 3 usually shows two peaks.

differs.how: Gen 3 mirrors usually show two peaks

us-Znxn.title: Landscape: marshy ponds and grasses (potholes)
us-Znxn.summary: From the northern border to the western Great Lakes: low wetlands with marshy grass and small shallow ponds, called prairie potholes.

us-a1wL.title: Map: population density, denser in the east
us-a1wL.summary: Areas east of the Missouri river are more densely populated than areas to the west.

us-a8x9.title: Landscape: moderate mountains, conifers
us-a8x9.summary: The Black Hills in the far west of South Dakota and east of Wyoming: moderately tall, conifer-covered mountains with rock outcrops, surrounded by flatter, less wooded land. Looks like parts of the Rockies.

us-a9Az.title: Sign: speed limit says "Speed Limit"
us-a9Az.summary: Speed signs read "Speed Limit" with fairly low numbers (miles), and limits ending in 5 are common. Canada's say "Maximum" and use higher km/h numbers.

differs.how: Canadian signs say "Maximum", with higher km/h numbers

us-a9s6.title: Landscape: dry plains up to tall mountains
us-a9s6.summary: Tall, sometimes snowy mountains behind dry, grassy, slightly shrubby plains. The tallest are in the centre-west, more gradual rocky hills are farther north, and greener mountains are farther east.

us-aAVg.title: Traffic lights: hung from wires over junction
us-aAVg.summary: Many big intersections in Michigan hang traffic lights and signs from wires across the middle, often in yellow boxes. Not unique, but most common there.

us-ak-1Olq.title: Google car: Gen 4 near the largest city
us-ak-1Olq.summary: Gen 4 coverage is concentrated around the largest city, Anchorage.

us-ak-2Lfw.title: Coverage: tall snow-covered mountains in view
us-ak-2Lfw.summary: Much of the coverage shows tall, snow-covered mountains.

us-ak-9qqo.title: Landscape: cold dead land, overcast
us-ak-9qqo.summary: The northernmost town covered: a cold, barren landscape under overcast sky with no tall buildings. A second Google car is sometimes visible.

us-ak-Cyms.title: Road: foggy rainy weather in Gen 2
us-ak-Cyms.summary: A highway from the Yukon border is recognised by foggy, rainy weather in Gen 2. The Canadian side nearby has similar weather but is mostly paved and has no outer lines.

us-ak-DVQ7.title: Google car: Gen 2 is fairly common here
us-ak-DVQ7.summary: Gen 2 is rare across the US, but Alaska has a fair amount.

us-ak-DnwM.title: Coverage: three isolated towns, backpack only
us-ak-DnwM.summary: Three isolated towns are covered only by backpack camera. The carrier's lime green hat or black-and-white beanie shows; the black-and-white bandana appears only in one of them.

us-ak-IDWK.title: Fire hydrants: pale pink or pale yellow
us-ak-IDWK.summary: Fire hydrants in the largest city are typically pale pink or pale yellow.

us-ak-Lm2l.title: Trees: thinner, narrower-leaved than elsewhere
us-ak-Lm2l.summary: Trees are generally thinner and have less broad leaves than those in the other 49 states.

us-ak-M50F.title: Sign: highway shield with the Big Dipper
us-ak-M50F.summary: The highway shield has the Big Dipper constellation at the bottom left.

us-ak-MBny.title: Road: gravel highway in Gen 2, lower mountains
us-ak-MBny.summary: Another gravel highway running east to west in Gen 2, like the previous one, but with noticeably lower mountains alongside.

us-ak-MD84.title: Road: gravel highway in Gen 2 with wildflowers
us-ak-MD84.summary: A mostly gravel highway across central mountains running east to west, in Gen 2 shot in late summer, so wildflowers and green shrubs are common.

us-ak-MbP1.title: Landscape: built-up town ringed by forested mountains
us-ak-MbP1.summary: The capital is the largest town in the panhandle and much more built up than the others, surrounded by heavily forested mountains and hills.

us-ak-S3bK.title: Vegetation: subarctic, little undergrowth
us-ak-S3bK.summary: Most of the interior and north is subarctic or tundra: little undergrowth in the forest and shorter trees.

us-ak-SXUe.title: Cities: only two major urban areas
us-ak-SXUe.summary: The only two major urban areas are Anchorage and Fairbanks.

us-ak-TQHg.title: Landscape: tall green forested mountains
us-ak-TQHg.summary: Towns in the southeastern archipelago near the British Columbia border: tall mountains with lush green forest behind, mostly wooden buildings, and often overcast, misty Gen 2. Coastal Oregon and Washington can look similar.

us-ak-VTst.title: Landscape: flat, snowy, overcast
us-ak-VTst.summary: The north end of a long northern highway is flat and snowy under overcast sky, with a small ridge of hills to the west in places.

us-ak-eyVX.title: Google car: low camera, big round blur
us-ak-eyVX.summary: A Gen 4 "smallcam" mounted lower than usual, with a big round blur and a small bump at the front, and the front of the white car clearly visible. The blur can be see-through.

us-ak-iRys.title: Suburbs: wide roads, commercial strips
us-ak-iRys.summary: Most suburbs are around Anchorage, with wide roads, commercial areas, sometimes heavy traffic and mountains in the distance. Fairbanks has similar areas but fewer mountains.

us-ak-j6hw.title: Pipeline: big oil pipeline beside main roads
us-ak-j6hw.summary: The Alaska pipeline is usually visible from main roads. There is no similar pipeline anywhere else in the US.

us-ak-jGan.title: Google car: low-quality older camera
us-ak-jGan.summary: Alaska is the only state with plenty of older low-resolution coverage with faded colours and a large blur at the bottom of the image.

us-ak-lPaS.title: Plate: all-yellow, or yellow with orange circle
us-ak-lPaS.summary: The most common plate is all yellow. In Gen 4 you may also see one with a large orange circle in the middle. Front plates are required.

us-ak-mAUK.title: Trees: aspen, white bark and round leaves
us-ak-mAUK.summary: Aspens grow at lower elevations in the interior and south-central areas. White bark, rounded leaves.

us-ak-tYxw.title: Fields: farmland only in the far south
us-ak-tYxw.summary: Because of the cold, farm fields are mainly in the south, in one valley and on one peninsula.

us-ak-v4UX.title: Google car: low-quality camera only near two cities
us-ak-v4UX.summary: The older low-quality camera is only found around the two big cities and parts of the road between them. Some places may have been updated.

us-ak-wvid.title: Fire hydrants: bright yellow or multicoloured
us-ak-wvid.summary: Fire hydrants in the second city are bright yellow or a mix of colours, most often yellow and blue.

us-avXB.title: Signs: highway shield differs by state
us-avXB.summary: Each state has its own highway shield, and some are distinctive enough to recognise.

us-bFMK.title: Street names: number plus direction (600 South)
us-bFMK.summary: Streets in Utah and Idaho, especially in cities, are often named with a number and compass direction, like "600 South". It is rare in other western states.

us-bdkQ.title: Landscape: jagged rocky mountains, pines, snow
us-bdkQ.summary: The Rockies, from the Canadian border to northern New Mexico: jagged, rocky mountains with many pines and snow all year on the highest peaks. Some parts are dry with few trees.

us-c26l.title: Sign: white rectangular signs at junctions
us-c26l.summary: Rectangular white signs are sometimes seen at intersections in Virginia.

us-dSRB.title: Signpost: white reflector on stop sign
us-dSRB.summary: White reflectors on signposts are unique to Kansas, most often on rural stop signs.

us-eHVg.title: Landscape: tall dry peaks
us-eHVg.summary: A ridge of tall, dry peaks along the New Mexico and Texas border, with smaller flat-topped, shrubby foothills in nearby areas.

us-eKQc.title: Landscape: sand-brown eroded rock formations
us-eKQc.summary: Badlands National Park has distinct sand-brown eroded rock formations that sometimes look more rounded and paler.

us-f8WU.title: Trees: extremely tall conifers, dark bark
us-f8WU.summary: Douglas firs: very tall conifers with dark brown bark and dark green needles, mostly in the northwest, also northern California, Idaho and east to Montana. They also grow in British Columbia.

us-fDFh.title: Gas station: Wawa
us-fDFh.summary: A regional gas station and convenience store chain in the mid-Atlantic states and Florida, densest in New Jersey and the Philadelphia area.

us-fYC3.title: Google car: low camera, big round blur
us-fYC3.summary: A "smallcam" Gen 4 mounted lower than usual, with a big round blur and a small bump at the front. The blur can be see-through. If badly blurred you may see a mirror on the right side. Canada has it too.

us-fz5Q.title: Sign: rectangular junction sign with arrows
us-fz5Q.summary: Rectangular junction signs with one or two arrows. Canada uses diamond-shaped junction signs.

us-fzDT.title: Sign: signs mounted on two posts
us-fzDT.summary: Signs mounted on two posts are common in Michigan, Ohio, Minnesota and New York, though not all signs. Other states have them less often.

us-g6RJ.title: Landscape: low forested mountains
us-g6RJ.summary: A low mountain range in the east with forested hills and common beech and oak trees. Houses in the south have fewer storeys, and New England-style wood panelling, high roofs and porches are more common to the north.

us-gGzS.title: Street sign: fraction in a circle symbol
us-gGzS.summary: West Virginia sometimes has street signs with a symbol that looks like a fraction inside a circle.

us-gdFs.title: Water towers: tall, town name painted on
us-gdFs.summary: Tall water towers in towns sometimes have the town and state name painted on them, handy for guessing the region. Canada has them too.

us-ggsD.title: Pole: insulator raised on top
us-ggsD.summary: An insulator raised slightly on top of the pole, best seen on simple one-insulator poles. Points to the US or Canada, not Europe.

us-goZa.title: Plate: each state has its own design
us-goZa.summary: Every state has its own plate design, and some are recognisable even through blur.

us-h1bS.title: Gas station: Casey's
us-h1bS.summary: A popular gas station and convenience chain in the Midwest, Plains and parts of the Mid-South, with the most in Illinois, Iowa and Missouri.

us-h8ml.title: Road: grainy salt-and-pepper surface
us-h8ml.summary: Some rural roads in the upper Midwest have a similar grainy surface, but the colour varies. Most common in one state in the Midwest.

us-hMnP.title: Road line: raised markers either side of double line
us-hMnP.summary: Rectangular markers on both sides of the double yellow line are common in four large states. Other states with rectangular markers put them between the double lines. Beware of left-turn lanes.

us-hi-28eK.title: Landscape: deep red soil, rugged hills, jungle
us-hi-28eK.summary: The westernmost covered island has deep red soil and large rugged hills with lush jungle-like plants. Other islands have similar soil but less dense vegetation on the hills.

us-hi-2r6I.title: Vegetation: lush tropical, ferns and tall grass
us-hi-2r6I.summary: Lush, tropical plants, but the volcanic islands have a wide range of landscapes. Expect ferns, tall grass and flowers along the roadsides.

us-hi-5JxK.title: Coverage: small island of gravel roads
us-hi-5JxK.summary: A small island southwest of the second-largest one, covered only by backpack camera on gravel roads and dirt trails: dry shrubs, rolling hills and dark red soil, with a few buildings at the western end.

us-hi-6yCv.title: Landscape: hillier and greener east end
us-hi-6yCv.summary: The east of the island has a volcano, so it is hillier and a bit more vegetated than the western parts.

us-hi-7Hx9.title: Landscape: dry flat grassland
us-hi-7Hx9.summary: In the centre of the second-largest island: dry, somewhat flat grassland with one or both of the island's mountain ranges visible.

us-hi-DKg0.title: Landscape: the only urban-feeling town
us-hi-DKg0.summary: The largest town on the small, sparsely populated island is its only urban area, and the soil is somewhat red.

us-hi-Eg63.title: Landscape: grassy plains, volcanic rock
us-hi-Eg63.summary: The largest island, farthest southeast: rolling grassy plains and volcanic rock inland, with one or more volcanoes usually visible from the road.

us-hi-MOXl.title: Google car: distinct green blur
us-hi-MOXl.summary: A distinct green blur is only seen on one island, the one with the main city.

us-hi-N9Pk.title: Pole: thick yellow bands
us-hi-N9Pk.summary: Thick yellow bands sometimes appear on poles. Don't mix them up with California's three stripes.

us-hi-OxOs.title: Road numbers: first digit shows the island
us-hi-OxOs.summary: State highway numbers start with 1 or 2 on the Big Island, 3 on Maui, 4 on Molokai and Lanai, 5 on Kauai and 6 to 9 on Oahu. All four so-called interstates are on Oahu.

us-hi-UtV2.title: Trees: tall Cook pines
us-hi-UtV2.summary: A small, distinctive island with a volcano just east of the centre. Tall Cook pines are abundant there, and younger ones line some main roads.

us-hi-Xfnk.title: Landscape: volcanic soil, rocks
us-hi-Xfnk.summary: A well-known grid of roads built on the slope of a big volcano, with volcanic soil and rocks, volcanic plants along the roads, and road angles that give the area away.

us-hi-YRn2.title: Google car: Gen 2 or regular Gen 4 only on 3 islands
us-hi-YRn2.summary: Gen 2 and regular Gen 4 only exist on the three largest islands. The other islands only have Gen 3 or the low-camera Gen 4.

us-hi-Ympi.title: Google car: Gen 2 fairly common, esp. rural
us-hi-Ympi.summary: A fair amount of Gen 2 coverage compared to other states, especially on rural roads. Gen 2 has a low-quality camera and circular blurs above and below it.

us-hi-Ys6w.title: Landscape: deep red soil, volcano at east end
us-hi-Ys6w.summary: A sparsely populated island with deep red soil and a prominent volcano at its eastern end. In older Gen 3 the plants look very dry.

us-hi-a0eb.title: Vegetation: lush coast with trees and ferns
us-hi-a0eb.summary: Most towns on the largest island are on the coast, which is lusher with more trees and ferns than the interior.

us-hi-b650.title: City: only dense city with tall buildings
us-hi-b650.summary: The main city, on the south of its island, is by far the largest. Dense urban areas with tall buildings are always in or near it.

us-hi-bZoK.title: Sign: guitar-pick highway shield, yellow posts
us-hi-bZoK.summary: Highway shields look like a guitar pick with the number at the bottom, and most highway signs are on yellow posts.

us-hi-cqVl.title: Vegetation: lush coast, bananas and palms
us-hi-cqVl.summary: Coastal areas are noticeably more lush and green, with banana plants, palms and views of the mountains.

us-hi-lgKi.title: Landscape: sloping volcanoes
us-hi-lgKi.summary: Sloping volcanoes, rugged cliffs, hills, valleys and craters, combined with tropical vegetation.

us-hi-ljgc.title: Landscape: barren red rocky land above the clouds
us-hi-ljgc.summary: A unique barren, red rocky landscape at high altitude, where clouds are usually visible below you.

us-hi-mHA9.title: Language: Hawaiian, 8 consonants and okina
us-hi-mHA9.summary: The only state with its own language, though English dominates. Place names are Hawaiian, using only H, K, L, M, N, P, W and the ʻokina. Every word ends in a vowel, and vowels may have a macron.

us-hi-nRqi.title: Landscape: dry grass and shrub hills
us-hi-nRqi.summary: Near the coasts of the small island: hills with dry grass and shrubs, very rural with few buildings.

us-hi-o41E.title: Road line: reflector pattern 1-4-1
us-hi-o41E.summary: Raised reflectors in a repeating pattern: one reflector, then four close together, then one.

us-hi-or8v.title: Landscape: steep lush hills around a big city
us-hi-or8v.summary: The island southeast of the westernmost one has the main city and steep, lush hills seen from all over, especially in the suburbs.

us-hi-pKp1.title: Houses: 1-2 storey light wood, lava rock walls
us-hi-pKp1.summary: Modern homes are typically 1-2 storey wooden buildings in lighter colours, and many have retaining walls made of volcanic rock.

us-hi-rCfQ.title: Google car: white car with low camera on small islands
us-hi-rCfQ.summary: On the other islands the low-camera Gen 4 was a white car, and you can often see its unblurred hood and mirrors.

us-hi-rkwO.title: Road: forest road in flat land
us-hi-rkwO.summary: Rural roads through forest on flat land are common south of the main eastern town on the largest island. Mountain forests with red soil and Gen 3 point to the westernmost covered island.

us-hi-s9sz.title: Google car: black car with low camera on big islands
us-hi-s9sz.summary: On the three largest islands, the low-camera Gen 4 was a black car, and you can often see its unblurred hood and mirrors.

us-hi-vAwL.title: Google car: low camera, big round blur
us-hi-vAwL.summary: A lot of Gen 4 "smallcam" coverage, mounted lower than usual, with a big round blur and a small bump at the front and parts of the car visible. The blur can be see-through.

us-hi-x4W4.title: Plate: white with rainbow arc
us-hi-x4W4.summary: The most common plate is white with an arcing rainbow across the middle, sometimes visible through the blur. Front plates are required.

us-hi-xedC.title: Google car: stubby antenna on Gen 3
us-hi-xedC.summary: Most Gen 3 coverage shows a stubby antenna. It isn't always visible, so check other clues.

us-i0f7.title: Plants: Spanish moss
us-i0f7.summary: Greyish-white drapes of Spanish moss hang on trees in the Deep South.

us-i6uG.title: Supermarket: Piggly Wiggly
us-i6uG.summary: A supermarket found mostly in the Southeast, and also in Wisconsin.

us-iP7y.title: Restaurant: Whataburger
us-iP7y.summary: A hamburger chain across the south-central US, with Texas by far the most locations.

us-iftd.title: Sign: speed limit sign says just "Speed"
us-iftd.summary: In Oregon, speed signs often say just "Speed" instead of "Speed Limit".

us-ir1O.title: Bollard: white diamond reflector on top
us-ir1O.summary: The most common roadside bollard in South Dakota and Montana has a white diamond on top. Montana usually has one bolt on it, South Dakota two. It's a common design in many states, and rotated squares look like diamonds.

us-j2CG.title: Restaurant: Zaxby's chicken
us-j2CG.summary: A fast-food chicken chain most common in the Southeast, with a few pockets elsewhere such as Utah and Montana. Georgia has the most.

us-jDaH.title: Bollard: very long rectangular reflector on top
us-jDaH.summary: The most common bollard in Oregon has a very long rectangular reflector on top. California has similar ones.

us-jFoS.title: Landscape: steep mountains seen from far away
us-jFoS.summary: Mountains in the south-central area, steeper than the nearby Ozarks and easier to see from a distance.

us-jGVD.title: Sign: wordy white parking signs
us-jGVD.summary: White metal parking signs with red, green or black text, often with times and arrows. Canadian ones look similar but use more symbols and fewer words.

differs.how: Canadian parking signs use more symbols, fewer words

us-jNem.title: Bollard: white or brown post
us-jNem.summary: In Washington: a white or brown post with a white rectangle on the front and two smaller white or silver squares on the back.

us-jQ4N.title: Landscape: rolling grass-covered sand hills
us-jQ4N.summary: In the central-north of one Great Plains state: recognisable rolling hills covered with prairie grass.

us-kNBA.title: Plate: short plates
us-kNBA.summary: Short plates like most of the Americas, unlike Europe's long ones. About half of the states don't require front plates, which can help find the state.

us-kaMy.title: Sign: highway distances in kilometres
us-kaMy.summary: Interstate 19 in Arizona, from Tucson to the Mexican border, uses kilometres on exit and distance signs, the only such highway. Speed limits there are still in mph.

us-kbLP.title: Houses: old three-storey wooden triplexes
us-kbLP.summary: Older three-storey wooden houses, called stacked triplexes, are very common in northeastern cities, especially in New York, Connecticut, Rhode Island and Massachusetts. Somewhat common in Atlantic Canadian cities too.

us-lB5Q.title: Landscape: dense jungle-like forest
us-lB5Q.summary: In the far south of Florida between two big cities: dense, jungle-like forest with few people, and long straight roads.

us-lDC9.title: Trucks: long-nose semi trucks
us-lDC9.summary: Semi trucks have a long nose with the engine in front of the cab. European and Asian trucks are cabovers (driver on top of the engine, L-shaped). Only useful against Europe, as these trucks are found across the Americas.

differs.how: Australian and NZ trucks are a mix of both

us-lESA.title: Sign: white plate with state route number on top
us-lESA.summary: In Pennsylvania, rectangular white signs on signposts at intersections show the number of the state route that joins.

us-lgT6.title: Landscape: extremely flat, shrubby, farmland
us-lgT6.summary: Extremely flat land with shrubby trees and farm fields, near the Mexican border in the south.

us-ljDv.title: Road: ordinary roads paved in concrete
us-ljDv.summary: Concrete paving on regular roads is much more common in Iowa than elsewhere. Ignore it on bridges, highways and in cities.

us-lm-150010.title: Landscape: red soil across the South
us-lm-150010.summary: Red soil is everywhere in the South, from parts of Louisiana and Arkansas through Mississippi, Tennessee, Alabama, Georgia and the Carolinas to southern Virginia. The Oklahoma City area is also red.

us-lm-22782.title: Landscape: flat northern half of the island
us-lm-22782.summary: On Guam, the northern half of the island is mostly flat.

us-lm-22783.title: Landscape: hills in the southern half of island
us-lm-22783.summary: On Guam, hills are mostly in the southern half of the island.

us-lm-253371.title: Mailbox: vertical metal house number sign
us-lm-253371.summary: Rural and outer-suburb properties in Ohio, lower Michigan and Indiana often have a vertical metal sign with white numbers, usually blue or green and often fixed to the mailbox. Rare elsewhere.

us-lm-253403.title: Fences: red metal
us-lm-253403.summary: Red metal fences are very common in Oklahoma and nearby states, especially Kansas, Texas and Arkansas. Not 100% reliable, so look for other clues.

us-lm-253404.title: Road line: small rectangular bumps on centre line
us-lm-253404.summary: Little rectangular bumps on the centre lines are unique to Texas. Round bumps appear in other states, but rectangular ones only here.

us-lm-253405.title: Pole: white or yellow rectangular plates
us-lm-253405.summary: Rectangular white or yellow plates on the side of poles in eastern Massachusetts, Rhode Island and Connecticut. Very rare elsewhere.

us-lm-253406.title: Pole: plate with a round part on the side
us-lm-253406.summary: Alabama poles mostly have a plate with a round part at the side, which the author has seen nowhere else.

us-lm-253407.title: Road line: gaps in lines at raised markers
us-lm-253407.summary: In Ohio, road lines often have a gap where a raised pavement marker sits. It rarely appears elsewhere, e.g. Tennessee or New Jersey.

us-lm-253408.title: Road line: reflectors in the middle, no lines
us-lm-253408.summary: A small road with no lines but southern-style reflectors in the middle is most likely South Carolina. Elsewhere reflectors sit next to lines, though lines can be faded.

us-lm-253409.title: Road line: short fine lines among wide lines
us-lm-253409.summary: Short, thin lines between Oregon's usually wide road lines help tell it from Washington, which also uses wide lines. Similar lines exist elsewhere.

us-lm-253410.title: Signpost: yellow posts
us-lm-253410.summary: Yellow posts are common in Colorado and rarer in Utah and Texas, very rarely elsewhere. Not very consistent.

us-lm-253412.title: Bollard: very common in one state
us-lm-253412.summary: A bollard extremely common in Oregon and almost exclusive to it. In California it's rare and usually not exactly the same, e.g. a bigger white rectangle or not fully on top.

us-lm-253413.title: Bollard: white square on top
us-lm-253413.summary: A bollard with a white square on top is unique to Utah and Idaho. If the square isn't fully on top, it should be Idaho.

us-lm-253415.title: Bollard: green post
us-lm-253415.summary: Green bollards are common and almost unique to Idaho and Colorado, in different forms, not only the one in the picture.

us-lm-253416.title: Bollard: rectangle on top, white or yellow
us-lm-253416.summary: Rectangle-topped bollards in Idaho, the only place in the western US with them. The rectangle can be white or yellow. Montana has a similar yellow one with a much larger reflector.

us-lm-253417.title: Signpost: side post next to the sign
us-lm-253417.summary: A signpost on the side of the sign, as in the picture, is unique to Iowa within the Plains and Midwest.

us-lm-253418.title: Bollard: black-capped, on guardrails
us-lm-253418.summary: Pennsylvania bollards are very common on guardrails and sometimes elsewhere. White or yellow, recognisable by shape and a black cap.

us-lm-253419.title: Guardrail: white bollard with grey or yellow square
us-lm-253419.summary: A white bollard with a grey or yellow square, unique to Texas among guardrails in the southern US.

us-lm-253420.title: Guardrail: no reflectors inside the rail
us-lm-253420.summary: Oklahoma has no guardrails with reflectors inside them. If you see a guardrail with reflectors, don't guess Oklahoma.

us-lm-253421.title: Guardrail: vertical yellow and black end
us-lm-253421.summary: Guardrail ends in Alabama have vertical yellow and black patterns, which sets them apart from other southern states.

us-lm-270713.hide: no learnable content (maximum speed limit map only)

us-lm-3647.title: Landscape: looks like Brazil or Kenya around a lake
us-lm-3647.summary: Around a lake by downtown Oklahoma City, the landscape suddenly looks like Brazil or Kenya, so don't be fooled.

us-lm-489977.title: Pole: vertical silver or gold plate at base
us-lm-489977.summary: In Rhode Island and Massachusetts, silver or gold-coloured vertical plates often sit near the base of utility poles.

us-lm-489978.title: Pole: yellow mesh near the base
us-lm-489978.summary: In southeastern Pennsylvania, utility poles often have a yellow mesh or net near the base.

us-lm-54750.title: Suburbs: wide roads, flatter, fewer mountains
us-lm-54750.summary: Suburban areas with wide roads, shops and sometimes heavy traffic, but flatter than around the largest city: the second city's suburbs.

us-lm-54766.title: Landscape: roadsides full of fireweed
us-lm-54766.summary: A peninsula recognised by masses of fireweed along the roads, mostly Gen 3 in autumn. Along the main highway you often see a bay to the west with mountains beyond.

us-lm-562505.title: Landscape: wide, flat volcano at the east end
us-lm-562505.summary: A rather flat, wide volcano with a unique shape, at the east end of one small island.

us-lm-578678.title: Landscape: houses built up the hillsides
us-lm-578678.summary: Most island houses sit on flat plains. Houses up on hillsides point to the mountain range in eastern Oahu, often Honolulu's suburbs.

us-lm-578679.title: Sign: street sign with tab and short arrow
us-lm-578679.summary: A tab above the street sign holding a short or very short arrow is almost unique to Oahu.

us-lm-578680.title: Sign: street sign with arrow, no tab
us-lm-578680.summary: No tab above the sign, with the arrow on the sign itself. Unique to Oahu.

us-lm-578681.title: Sign: plain street sign with only the name
us-lm-578681.summary: A basic street sign with only the road name, mostly on the Big Island, rare on Kauai and extremely rare on Oahu and Maui.

us-lm-578682.title: Sign: plain street sign with number under Rd/St
us-lm-578682.summary: A basic street sign with a number below the abbreviation (Rd, St, Pl), unique to Kauai.

us-lm-578683.title: Sign: empty tab above street sign
us-lm-578683.summary: A tab above the sign with nothing in it, found in the Maui district: Maui, Lanai and Molokai.

us-lm-578684.title: Sign: tab above street sign with long arrow
us-lm-578684.summary: A tab above the sign holding a long arrow, found in the Maui district: Maui, Lanai and Molokai.

us-lm-595852.title: Sign: 2-digit number and dash (tax zone)
us-lm-595852.summary: Signs on Oahu, and sometimes elsewhere, often show a 2-digit number and a dash for tax zones. They aren't used in urban Honolulu, start at 41 on the east coast and increase counter-clockwise.

us-lm-595862.title: Landscape: lush town with grid roads
us-lm-595862.summary: A lush, somewhat built-up coastal town with a grid layout of many roads, with a big mountain sometimes visible to the west. Other grids on the island look very different.

us-lm-595863.title: Landscape: lots of volcanic rock
us-lm-595863.summary: The Big Island has the only active volcano and is the newest island, so volcanic rock is common.

us-lm-595864.title: Road angle: roads run southeast to northwest
us-lm-595864.summary: A surprisingly good clue for the western Big Island: roads angled southeast to northwest.

us-lm-595865.title: Landscape: big mountain rising east of the west coast
us-lm-595865.summary: A large mountain, Hualalai, rises to the east of the Kona area.

us-lm-595866.title: Plants: planted eucalyptus above the ocean
us-lm-595866.summary: The northeast coast of the Big Island has planted eucalyptus overlooking the ocean.

us-lm-595867.title: Road: looks like Mars, big volcanic rocks
us-lm-595867.summary: A road that looks like Mars with large volcanic rocks on its sides. Unlike a similar red hill road, it has no centre lines.

us-lm-595868.title: Landscape: neighbouring islands visible to the west
us-lm-595868.summary: On the west coast of the second-largest island you can often see two other islands to the west. In the north, a mountain range rises to the east.

us-lm-595869.title: Road: narrow, lush coastal highway
us-lm-595869.summary: A narrow, lush coastal highway in the north of Maui. Some parts have centre lines, which can be a toss-up with the Big Island, but it is narrower with very narrow shoulders.

us-lm-595870.title: Landscape: foothills looking over the island
us-lm-595870.summary: The area near Kula sits at the foot of a big volcano and often looks over the rest of the island.

us-lm-595871.title: Road: narrow, open, south coast visible
us-lm-595871.summary: The south part of the narrow coastal highway: fairly open land, and you can often see the south coast because no trees block the view. Same toss-up caveats as the north.

us-lm-595872.title: Road: volcanic rock with water directly to the south
us-lm-595872.summary: The road around and east of Seaview on the Big Island combines a volcanic rock landscape with the ocean immediately to the south.

us-lm-595873.title: Rail: elevated railway
us-lm-595873.summary: The only elevated railway in Hawaii is on Oahu. It mostly follows one highway, merges into the interstate and goes on to the airport.

us-lm-628557.title: Road names: painted on the sidewalk
us-lm-628557.summary: In San Francisco almost every intersection has the road name painted on the sidewalk, so streets stay labelled after earthquakes knock signs down.

us-lm-628558.title: Cars: Waymo robotaxis with lidar on top
us-lm-628558.summary: Waymo is a self-driving taxi company. Its cars have a lidar on top and nobody behind the wheel. As of Dec 2025 it operates in San Francisco, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Austin and Atlanta.

us-lm-628563.title: Houses: horizontal overlapping boards
us-lm-628563.summary: Houses in the northeast often have walls of horizontal, overlapping boards.

us-lm-628577.title: Cars: Zoox robotaxis, distinct shape, no driver
us-lm-628577.summary: Zoox is a robotaxi service with very distinctive, driverless cars. As of Dec 2025 it operates in San Francisco and Las Vegas.

us-lm-628590.title: Plants: cabbage palmetto (sabal palm)
us-lm-628590.summary: Sabal palmetto is native to subtropical coasts of Florida, Georgia, South Carolina, southeastern North Carolina and extreme southern Texas.

us-lm-628591.title: Plants: California fan palm
us-lm-628591.summary: Washingtonia filifera, the only palm native to the western US and one of the largest native palms.

us-lm-628596.title: Plants: saw palmetto thickets
us-lm-628596.summary: Saw palmetto grows in clumps or dense thickets on sandy coasts and as undergrowth in pine woods, in coastal Florida and Georgia.

us-lm-628598.title: Pole: white paint at the bottom with street name
us-lm-628598.summary: At intersections in Key West, poles have white paint at the bottom with the street name on it.

us-lm-628599.title: Trees: gumbo limbo, red bark and twisting trunk
us-lm-628599.summary: The gumbo limbo has red bark and irregular, sometimes twisting trunks with oval green leaves. Only in coastal Florida south of Orlando and Tampa.

us-lm-628600.title: Bus: free orange-and-green trolley
us-lm-628600.summary: Greater Miami has a free trolley system, with each town using different colours. This one is orange on top and green below with a thin white stripe.

us-lm-628601.title: Bus: free blue trolley
us-lm-628601.summary: Another town's free trolley in the Greater Miami system is blue.

us-lm-628602.title: Buildings: fun
us-lm-628602.summary: Miami Modern architecture has playful, unconventional designs, decorative details, smooth corners, flat roofs and lots of glass, in certain districts of Miami and Miami Beach.

us-lm-636632.title: Signpost: wooden signposts
us-lm-636632.summary: Wooden signposts are mainly found in five northwestern states and in California.

us-lm-636647.title: Plate: no front plates in the south
us-lm-636647.summary: Cars without front plates are mostly south of a line from northern Arizona to North Carolina (except Texas), in Ohio and neighbours, Delaware and Oklahoma. Cars travel and not everyone follows the law, so use with caution.

us-lm-636648.title: Landscape: Midwest farms but very hilly
us-lm-636648.summary: A unique area in southwest Wisconsin with Midwestern features like farming, but very hilly.

us-lm-636650.title: Trees: quaking aspen, thin white bark
us-lm-636650.summary: Thin trees with white bark that often grow in groups. In the lower 48 they're in the northeast, around the Great Lakes (plus northeast Iowa), northern Idaho and scattered western spots.

us-lm-636651.title: Language: Spanish
us-lm-636651.summary: The most common non-English language, most common near Mexico in Texas, New Mexico, Arizona and California, and in Florida, where it's the most spoken language in one big county.

us-lm-636652.title: Language: double vowels and diacritics
us-lm-636652.summary: Navajo, spoken in the Navajo Nation in Arizona and New Mexico, is the biggest Native American language. It can be recognised by double vowels and diacritics.

us-lm-636653.title: Language: Cherokee syllabary script
us-lm-636653.summary: Cherokee is spoken in the Cherokee Nation in Oklahoma and parts of North Carolina, with its own distinctive writing system, the Cherokee syllabary.

us-lm-636654.title: Street signs: in Finnish as well as English
us-lm-636654.summary: In one town in Michigan's Upper Peninsula, street signs are in Finnish and English.

us-lm-642028.title: Trees: broad round oak crowns in mixed forest
us-lm-642028.summary: Eastern deciduous oaks in mixed forests: broad, rounded crowns forming a continuous canopy, bare thick limbs in winter, stout trunks with grey scaly to deeply cracked bark.

us-lm-647413.title: Forest: lush spruce
us-lm-647413.summary: Spruce and pine forests are common in the western US, from New Mexico, Colorado, Wyoming and Montana westward. The lush spruce type shown becomes more common near the Pacific coast.

us-lm-647416.title: Trees: southern live oak with Spanish moss
us-lm-647416.summary: Common in Florida and along the southern coast. Often has Spanish moss hanging from the branches, giving a pendulous look.

us-lm-647417.title: Trees: southern magnolia
us-lm-647417.summary: Only in the South, but not in southern Florida. Its range runs from around Orlando and Tampa to North Carolina and Texas.

us-lm-647418.title: Trees: balsam fir, symmetric, dark needles
us-lm-647418.summary: A very symmetric tree with fairly dark needles that often grows close to the ground. In the US it's in the northeast from northern New York and near the Great Lakes, at latitudes like Vermont and Maine.

us-lm-647419.title: Trees: buckeye
us-lm-647419.summary: Buckeyes are mostly in the east from Ohio down through West Virginia, Virginia and Kentucky to Tennessee and North Carolina, with some in Missouri. California is the only western state with them.

us-lm-647586.title: Vineyards: perfectly straight trellised rows
us-lm-647586.summary: Vineyards in perfectly straight rows of low or medium vines on posts and wires, with very clean ground between rows. Mainly California, Oregon and Washington, most often California.

us-lm-653313.title: Trees: dense round glossy evergreen
us-lm-653313.summary: Canyon live oak: an evergreen with a rounded, very dense dark-green crown that can look glossy, thick limbs, sometimes several trunks, and grey-brown scaly bark.

us-lm-662855.title: Landscape: rolling hills, firs and aspens
us-lm-662855.summary: New England landscapes vary a lot. Maine in particular can look a lot like Canada. Mostly rolling hills, with forests full of firs and aspens.

us-lm-662856.title: Coverage: winter or fall coverage
us-lm-662856.summary: Winter and fall coverage is common in New England, especially Massachusetts, Connecticut and Rhode Island. Winter coverage also exists in the South, so don't mix them up by vibes only.

us-lm-662857.title: Landscape: forested rolling hills
us-lm-662857.summary: Upstate New York and Pennsylvania are quite forested, and rolling hills are common.

us-lm-662858.title: Landscape: looks Midwestern but with more trees
us-lm-662858.summary: Some places in the mid-Atlantic look deceptively Midwestern, but with more trees.

us-lm-662859.title: Landscape: rural area that looks southern
us-lm-662859.summary: Rural New Jersey looks strikingly southern.

us-lm-662860.title: Buildings: lots of brick
us-lm-662860.summary: Brick buildings are more common in the mid-Atlantic than elsewhere, especially around Philadelphia.

us-lm-662861.title: Bollard: white plate with 6 bolts
us-lm-662861.summary: A white rectangular plate with 6 bolts: two at the top, two in the middle, two at the bottom. Variants have circular, rectangular or no reflectors. All are found in California.

us-lm-663170.title: Grassland: tall stiff tufts, scattered shrubs
us-lm-663170.summary: Open, thin grassland with tall, stiff tobosa tufts and lower grama patches, scattered shrubs. Common in the Chihuahuan desert: west Texas, southern New Mexico and southeast Arizona.

us-lm-663172.title: Crops: straight rows, corn wall in summer
us-lm-663172.summary: Large fields in perfectly straight rows. Corn forms a tall green wall in summer, soybeans a low dense carpet, and oats or barley stay shorter and turn golden before harvest.

us-lm-663173.title: Plants: Joshua tree, tree yucca with pom-poms
us-lm-663173.summary: A tree-like yucca with a woody trunk and thick candelabra arms. Each tip has a dense rosette of stiff, sharp leaves like green pom-poms, with an irregular outline.

us-lm-663377.title: Trees: giant redwood, tall straight
us-lm-663377.summary: Coast redwood: very tall trees in straight columns, with reddish-brown, very fibrous bark, in damp forest with ferns, moss and sometimes fog. Mostly the far north coast of California, sometimes southwest Oregon.

us-lm-665059.title: Trees: eastern hemlock
us-lm-665059.summary: A feathery conifer with a drooping top, small cones, in the northeast and Appalachians in cool damp valleys. Needles lie in two rows, unlike the western hemlock, which grows with moss, ferns and giants like Douglas fir.

us-lm-667513.title: Trees: wind-bent dense dark conifer, flat top
us-lm-667513.summary: Monterey cypress: a coastal conifer with very dense dark-green scale-like foliage, shaped by the wind into a flat crown with long branches bent one way, like a horizontal umbrella. A clue for a windy, foggy coast in central California.

us-lm-684193.title: Coverage: winter coverage in the Appalachians
us-lm-684193.summary: Within the Appalachians, winter coverage is most common in West Virginia.

us-lm-684256.title: Landscape: mix of Appalachian and Southern look
us-lm-684256.summary: Tennessee and Kentucky look like a mix of Appalachian and Southern landscape.

us-lm-684257.title: Landscape: flat and marshy
us-lm-684257.summary: Flat, marshy landscapes are common in Louisiana.

us-lm-684258.title: Traffic lights: horizontal layout
us-lm-684258.summary: Horizontal traffic lights are common in Nebraska, New Mexico, Texas and Louisiana, and appear occasionally in Oklahoma and Georgia.

us-lm-684259.title: Billboards: banned in four states
us-lm-684259.summary: Billboards are banned in Maine, Vermont, Alaska and Hawaii, so seeing one rules those out.

us-lm-684260.title: Supermarket: Food Lion
us-lm-684260.summary: Mostly between Maryland and South Carolina, sometimes in Tennessee, Georgia and West Virginia.

us-lm-684261.title: Shops: Dunkin' not in the northwest
us-lm-684261.summary: Dunkin' Donuts isn't found in states northwest of South Dakota.

us-lm-684262.title: Gas stations: BP missing from large areas
us-lm-684262.summary: BP isn't found in the West (from Kansas on), Louisiana, Arkansas, or upstate New York to Maine.

us-lm-684263.title: Supermarket: Kroger missing from some areas
us-lm-684263.summary: Kroger isn't found from Nebraska to Minnesota, in Pennsylvania or northeast of it, Florida or Oklahoma.

us-lm-684264.title: Supermarket: Aldi in the east
us-lm-684264.summary: Aldi is found in the eastern half from about mid Texas, but not in Maine. In the west only California and around Phoenix.

us-lm-685991.title: Plants: tall fan palm with skirt of dead fronds
us-lm-685991.summary: A thick single-trunk palm with a hanging skirt of dead fronds, grey-green fan leaves with white threads, forming groves at oases. Untrimmed, the skirt reaches almost the ground.

us-lm-685992.title: Plants: sword fern in big radial clumps
us-lm-685992.summary: A glossy dark-green evergreen fern in large radial clumps with stiff, arching sword-like fronds (0.5-1.5 m), covering the understory under damp northwestern conifers.

us-lm-686225.title: Plants: straight single-trunk palm
us-lm-686225.summary: A palm with a straight single trunk, sometimes with spiky leaf bases, sometimes smooth, a compact crown of fan leaves and dead fronds hanging as a skirt if untrimmed.

us-lm-686226.title: Plants: low trunkless palm in dense clumps
us-lm-686226.summary: A low, nearly trunkless palm in dense round clumps with stiff green to silvery fan leaves, often carpeting the ground under open pine woods.

us-lm-686227.title: Plants: slender grey palm with ringed trunk
us-lm-686227.summary: A slender single-trunk palm with a grey ringed trunk and circular fan leaves with drooping tips and silvery undersides. Native to the Florida Keys, most likely in south Florida, sometimes planted elsewhere in the state.

us-lm-686228.title: Plants: giant blue-green ribbed cactus
us-lm-686228.summary: A giant blue-green columnar cactus with strong vertical ribs and fine spines, growing candelabra-like arms with age, dominating open flats and slopes of the Sonoran desert.

us-lm-700521.title: Windshield sticker: required sticker in the capital
us-lm-700521.summary: Cars registered in Washington DC must have this sticker on the windshield.

us-lm-700522.title: Sign: exit sign combined with speed limit
us-lm-700522.summary: New Alabama coverage can have exit signs combined with a speed limit.

us-lm-700523.title: Marker: mile marker hanging from overpass
us-lm-700523.summary: In Alabama, mile markers hang from overpasses.

us-lm-700524.title: Overpass: stripes glued to support pillars
us-lm-700524.summary: Alabama often has stripes stuck on overpass support pillars.

us-lm-700525.title: Street sign: red street name signs
us-lm-700525.summary: In the western part of Mesa, next to Phoenix, red street name signs are sometimes used.

us-lm-700527.title: Marker: white postmile with county abbreviation
us-lm-700527.summary: Instead of mile markers, California uses postmile markers that are white, not green, and carry a county abbreviation.

us-lm-700528.title: Marker: bridge marker with many numbers
us-lm-700528.summary: California posts bridge markers with lots of numbers on bridges. The county abbreviations on them differ from those on the postmile markers.

us-lm-700529.title: Google car: unique car north of a famous bridge
us-lm-700529.summary: A unique Google car can be found north of the Golden Gate Bridge, in the San Francisco area.

us-lm-700530.title: Google car: unique car on an island
us-lm-700530.summary: An island south of Los Angeles has its own unique Google car.

us-lm-700531.title: Street sign: with a tree on it
us-lm-700531.summary: Oakland has an oak tree on its street name signs.

us-lm-700532.title: Landscape: palm trees everywhere vs hardly any
us-lm-700532.summary: Northern California differs from southern in palm trees: you see palms everywhere around LA but hardly any around the San Francisco Bay Area.

us-lm-700533.title: Landscape: tropical feel, spread-out houses
us-lm-700533.summary: Los Angeles and San Diego feel more tropical, with more spread-out houses than the compact, dense feel of San Francisco.

us-lm-700534.title: Landscape: barren desert outside the big cities
us-lm-700534.summary: Southern California outside the major cities is a barren desert.

us-lm-700535.title: Landscape: marshy, tropical, many palms
us-lm-700535.summary: South Florida is marshy and tropical with lots of palm trees.

us-lm-700536.title: Landscape: sandier soil, more pines than palms
us-lm-700536.summary: Central Florida has slightly sandier soil, and more pines than palms, though palms still appear.

us-lm-700537.title: Landscape: small round shallow lakes
us-lm-700537.summary: Small circular shallow lakes are especially common in central Florida around Lakeland and Orlando.

us-lm-700538.title: Coverage: lots of backpack coverage at a theme park
us-lm-700538.summary: GeoGuessr's official maps favour backpack coverage, so on the official US map or state streaks expect a lot of it at Disney World in Orlando.

us-lm-700539.title: Landscape: sandy soil, pines, few palms
us-lm-700539.summary: North Florida has sandier soil and rarely palm trees. Forests are mostly pine and the feel is more like Florida's northern neighbours.

us-lm-701572.title: Trees: red pine, straight reddish trunk
us-lm-701572.summary: Red pine: a conifer of the northern US and Canada with a straight reddish trunk and an open, airy crown with gaps. Common in cold forests and plantations around the Great Lakes.

us-lm-706207.title: Sign: no-parking signs along freeway exit ramps
us-lm-706207.summary: Georgia likes to decorate its freeway exit ramps with no-parking signs.

us-lm-706209.title: Google car: backpack camera in a park
us-lm-706209.summary: A backpack camera all over a park in Columbus, Indiana.

us-lm-706210.title: Marker: blue square on a post
us-lm-706210.summary: This kind of blue square on a post is exclusive to Indiana.

us-lm-706211.title: Google car: unique car on a forest road
us-lm-706211.summary: A stretch of road in a national forest near Beattyville, Kentucky, has a unique Google car. The coverage may be overwritten.

us-lm-706212.title: Sign: word "parish" instead of county
us-lm-706212.summary: Louisiana calls counties parishes, from its French colonial past, and the word may show on intersection signs. No other state uses it that way.

us-lm-706213.title: Windshield sticker: four small squares
us-lm-706213.summary: A windshield sticker in Louisiana with four smaller squares inside it.

us-lm-706214.title: Windshield sticker: circular
us-lm-706214.summary: A circular windshield sticker found in New Orleans, Louisiana.

us-lm-706215.title: Sign: ice warning signs
us-lm-706215.summary: Signs warning about ice are common in Louisiana.

us-lm-706216.title: Sign: thicker black stripes on chevron sign
us-lm-706216.summary: The black stripes on these black-and-yellow signs are a bit thicker in Louisiana than in other states.

us-lm-719854.title: Road line: dashed single yellow centre line
us-lm-719854.summary: Maine often uses a dashed single yellow centre line, or dashed plus solid, instead of a solid double, a bit more often than neighbouring states.

us-lm-719855.title: Windshield sticker: one edge or chunk missing
us-lm-719855.summary: Maine inspection stickers come in various colours, but all have one edge or a chunk of one side missing.

us-lm-719856.title: Sign: green US route shield with "business"
us-lm-719856.summary: A green US route shield with the word "business" on top, unique to Maryland.

us-lm-719857.title: Overpass: code painted on interstate bridges
us-lm-719857.summary: Some interstate bridges in Maryland, but not neighbouring states or DC, have a code painted on them.

us-lm-719858.title: Windshield sticker: three white rectangles
us-lm-719858.summary: Three white rectangles: the central one horizontal with a number, the left and right ones vertical.

us-lm-719859.title: Overpass: green plaque with white numbers
us-lm-719859.summary: Overpass bridges in Mississippi have green plaques with white numbers.

us-lm-719860.title: Sign: yellow direction box
us-lm-719860.summary: The yellow direction box is only found in Mississippi.

us-lm-719861.title: Sign: unique county route shield
us-lm-719861.summary: The county containing Las Vegas uses a unique county route shield.

us-lm-719862.title: Marker: mile marker with highway, county, mile
us-lm-719862.summary: Nevada mile marker: the top shows the highway name, the middle a county abbreviation and the bottom the mile number.

us-lm-719863.title: Sign: interstate sign with a dividing line
us-lm-719863.summary: These interstate signs, with a dividing line between the two numbers, should only be found in New Hampshire.

us-lm-719864.title: Sign: US route sign with a dividing line
us-lm-719864.summary: These US route signs, with a dividing line, are also specific to New Hampshire.

us-lm-719865.title: Windshield sticker: number in white box
us-lm-719865.summary: A number in a white rectangle with a thick colourful border (New Hampshire).

us-lm-719866.title: Windshield sticker: coloured post-it with black number
us-lm-719866.summary: Old New Hampshire stickers look like colourful post-its with a black number.

us-lm-719867.title: Road numbers: 3-digit starting with 5, unique
us-lm-719867.summary: New Jersey 500-series county routes have unique 3-digit numbers starting with 5, one route per number statewide, and follow the same even-west-east, odd-north-south rule as interstates.

us-lm-719868.title: Windshield sticker: three rectangles with numbers
us-lm-719868.summary: Three rectangles, each with a number. The outer ones make a year (like 2023) and are filled with a colour; the central one has a white background and one digit.

us-lm-719869.title: Place names: ending in -kill
us-lm-719869.summary: New York place names often end in -kill (Catskill, Cobleskill), from the Middle Dutch word for stream, a leftover of the 17th-century Dutch colony.

us-lm-719870.title: Windshield sticker: one number each side
us-lm-719870.summary: One number on the left and one on the right with a long white gap between them.

us-lm-719871.title: Transport: streetcar in one big city
us-lm-719871.summary: Charlotte has a streetcar system, unlike Raleigh.

us-lm-719872.title: Sign: green parking signs vs blue
us-lm-719872.summary: Charlotte uses green parking signs, while Raleigh uses blue ones.

us-lm-719874.title: Sign: circular pay-to-park signs
us-lm-719874.summary: Raleigh, NC uses circular pay-to-park signs to mark parking meters, unlike Charlotte.

us-lm-719875.title: Reflectors: circular reflectors
us-lm-719875.summary: These circular reflectors are found in Pittsburgh.

us-lm-719876.title: Overpass: clearance posted on every one
us-lm-719876.summary: South Carolina is the only southeastern state that posts the clearance on every overpass.

us-lm-719877.title: Overpass: black-and-white stripes on supports
us-lm-719877.summary: Black and white stripes on overpass supports are a dead giveaway for South Carolina. Sometimes a yellow-and-black striped sign is used instead.

us-lm-728571.title: Landscape: isolated striking rock peak
us-lm-728571.summary: A striking, isolated rock peak in northwestern New Mexico, visible from up to 40 km, a good clue for the region. Similar formations nearby don't have a long, low stone wall next to them.

us-lm-728573.title: Symbol: three stars, also black and white
us-lm-728573.summary: A three-star symbol found in many places in Tennessee, including historical place signs. It's from the state flag but can also be black and white.

us-lm-728574.title: Sign: unique city font
us-lm-728574.summary: Chattanooga has its own font on some signs in the city.

us-lm-728575.title: Bins: trash bins with city logo
us-lm-728575.summary: Nashville has trash bins with a recognisable logo.

us-lm-728576.title: Marker: mile marker with two numbers
us-lm-728576.summary: Tennessee state routes have mile markers where the larger number is the mile (resetting at county borders) and the smaller bottom number is the state route.

us-lm-728577.title: Decoration: lone star on gates
us-lm-728577.summary: Texas, the Lone Star State, shows its star on its flag, and many Texans use it as decoration, for example on gates.

us-lm-728578.title: Traffic lights: yellow with black border
us-lm-728578.summary: Within Texas, yellow traffic lights with black borders appear in Dallas, Fort Worth and San Antonio.

us-lm-728579.title: Traffic lights: fully black
us-lm-728579.summary: Within Texas, completely black traffic lights are in Dallas and Houston.

us-lm-728580.title: Traffic lights: fully yellow
us-lm-728580.summary: Within Texas, fully yellow traffic lights are in San Antonio, El Paso and Austin.

us-lm-728581.title: Windshield sticker: MMYY in white box with border
us-lm-728581.summary: A month-year number (like 1022) in a white rectangle with a colourful border.

us-lm-728582.title: Windshield sticker: orange T in a circle
us-lm-728582.summary: A windshield sticker with an orange T in a circle, found exclusively in Dallas.

us-lm-728583.title: Farmland: circles from centre pivot irrigation
us-lm-728583.summary: The circles seen in satellite view are made by giant centre pivot irrigation machines, visible from a distance, in many regions of the country.

us-lm-802381.title: Sign: guitar-pick route shield with number
us-lm-802381.summary: A guitar-pick shaped route sign with the road number inside.

us-lm-802382.title: Sign: state-outline-of-stars route shield
us-lm-802382.summary: A route shield showing the state outline made of stars with the road number inside, a replica of the state flag.

us-mJxO.title: Houses: adobe, rounded edges, flat roofs
us-mJxO.summary: Pueblo Revival houses in New Mexico: sand-brown adobe or brick and concrete with rounded edges and flat roofs. Some in Arizona and Colorado.

us-mVMG.title: Buildings: brownstone row houses
us-mVMG.summary: Brownstone row houses or government buildings of brick and sandstone, found in dense northeastern cities and in one big Midwest city.

us-mvHr.title: Sign: black one-way arrow with "ONE WAY"
us-mvHr.summary: A horizontal black rectangle with a white arrow and always the words "ONE WAY". In cities it's a white vertical sign with the text and an arrow below. Canada's has the same shape but may lack the words.

differs.how: Canadian one-way signs may not say "ONE WAY"

us-ntS3.title: Supermarket: Publix
us-ntS3.summary: A regional supermarket chain mainly in Florida and nearby parts of the Deep South.

us-oxdW.title: Road line: no centre line, just white edges
us-oxdW.summary: Some small roads in California and Kentucky have no yellow centre line, only solid white lines on each side. It rarely appears in other states.

us-qWZp.title: Supermarket: ShopRite
us-qWZp.summary: A regional supermarket chain in six northeastern and mid-Atlantic states: Connecticut, New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Delaware and Maryland.

us-qnm6.title: Sign: triangle reading "No Passing Zone"
us-qnm6.summary: A yellow triangle sign with the words "No Passing Zone", found only here.

us-rLEY.title: Landscape: lone tall butte standing alone
us-rLEY.summary: In far northeast Wyoming, a very tall, standalone butte rises from the land and can be seen from miles away because there are no nearby mountains.

us-rPvm.title: Crops: rice, flat low-prairie fields
us-rPvm.summary: Rice is grown in few areas, so it's a very useful clue. Large flat fields like low prairie, only in north-central California and the lower Mississippi valley.

us-rRBK.title: Trees: Eastern White Pine, layered branches
us-rRBK.summary: A graceful pine with horizontal layered branches that curve up at the ends. Common in the northeast, northern Midwest near the Great Lakes and the Appalachians, and also in eastern Canada.

us-rZEx.title: Plants: saguaro cactus, tall tube with arms
us-rZEx.summary: Tall, straight tube-shaped cacti with a few branches, found in southern Arizona near the Mexican border.

us-ri5Z.title: Restaurant: Waffle House
us-ri5Z.summary: A regional chain mainly in the South and Southeast, with a few in the Midwest and mid-Atlantic. Georgia has the most.

us-rwXR.title: Road line: rectangular raised pavement markers
us-rwXR.summary: Rectangular raised markers on the road, found in the south and west, and in one northeastern state.

us-rxbf.title: Roofs: red metal
us-rxbf.summary: Buildings with red metal roofs are most common in the Mid-South and southern Appalachians: Virginia, West Virginia, Ohio, Kentucky, Tennessee, Arkansas and North Carolina. They appear elsewhere too.

us-sJCE.title: Buildings: Baptist churches
us-sJCE.summary: Baptist churches are very common, especially in the southern plains and southeast. They are rare in Canada.

us-tH7v.title: Bollard: white square on top of black rectangle
us-tH7v.summary: A bollard with a white square reflector above a black rectangle reflector, unique to Utah.

us-tLW4.title: Landmark: hexagonal brick fort with moat
us-tLW4.summary: The main island of Dry Tortugas park has a hexagonal brick fort with a moat. The lighthouse on the other key has a brown top and white bottom, bright concrete path and palms.

us-tVFe.title: Pole: three yellow stripes at the bottom
us-tVFe.summary: Most of California has poles with three yellow stripes at the base, except two northeastern counties. A city in Oregon has the same.

us-tzrp.title: Landscape: very flat, red soil, crops
us-tzrp.summary: A very flat, open river valley with red soil in the mid-south, with corn and other crops.

us-uWKN.title: Landscape: forested rolling ridges
us-uWKN.summary: Forest-covered rolling hills with flat valleys between them. Most ridges run from southwest to northeast.

us-v4sG.title: Landscape: golden agricultural fields
us-v4sG.summary: Golden farm fields are common in the northwest. Flat parts of the next state to the south look similar.

us-vhEL.title: Houses: on short stilts, 1-3 feet up
us-vhEL.summary: Houses on short concrete or wooden stilts, 1-3 feet off the ground, are common on the western and central Gulf Coast near the sea and rivers.

us-wGfP.title: Sign: white signs attached to signposts
us-wGfP.summary: White signs attached to signposts are common in North Carolina.

us-wJ5Q.title: Signs: Adopt-a-Highway signs
us-wJ5Q.summary: Most states have their own Adopt-a-Highway roadside signs that can be learned. Designs vary slightly within some states.

us-wUyE.title: Pole: wooden poles, big cylinder transformers
us-wUyE.summary: Mostly wooden utility poles. Large metal cylinder transformers on them never appear in Europe, where concrete poles are more typical.

us-xDsS.title: Trees: tall southern pines, fluffy needles
us-xDsS.summary: Loblolly and longleaf pines are tall with fluffy clusters of needles. They are abundant in the southeast and mostly limited to it.

us-y54R.title: Bollard: reflector on a thin stick
us-y54R.summary: A reflector on a thin stick: a vertical rectangle with a white centre and black outline. Found in Nevada.

us-yWN6.title: Landscape: dense forest east and north
us-yWN6.summary: Tree cover is much denser in the east and north than in the west and southwest.

us-z0ci.title: Sign: blue services sign before exits
us-z0ci.summary: Big blue rectangular signs with white text before exits show food, lodging and fuel. Canada has similar signs on some highways.
